Compute \(|P|\) with \(P=\begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & \alpha \\ 3 & -5 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\):

Entry \(q_{23}=k\,(P^{-1})_{23}=k\cdot\dfrac{C_{32}}{|P|}\), where \(C_{32}=(-1)^{3+2}\det\begin{bmatrix}3 & -2 \\ 2 & \alpha\end{bmatrix}=-(3\alpha+4)\).
Given \(q_{23}=-\dfrac{k}{8}\):

Equate: \(12\alpha+20=24\alpha+32\Rightarrow \alpha=-1\). Then \(|P|=12(-1)+20=8=2k\Rightarrow k=4\).

Let \(x_i=P(B_i)\) and \(p=(1-x_1)(1-x_2)(1-x_3)\). By independence, \(\alpha=x_1(1-x_2)(1-x_3)=p\cdot\dfrac{x_1}{1-x_1}\), and similarly \(\beta=p\cdot\dfrac{x_2}{1-x_2}\), \(\gamma=p\cdot\dfrac{x_3}{1-x_3}\). Write \(a=\dfrac{x_1}{1-x_1},\; b=\dfrac{x_2}{1-x_2},\; c=\dfrac{x_3}{1-x_3}\), so \(\alpha=pa,\ \beta=pb,\ \gamma=pc\).

The relation \((\alpha-2\beta)p=\alpha\beta\) gives \(p^2(a-2b)=p^2ab\Rightarrow a-2b=ab\Rightarrow \dfrac1b-\dfrac2a=1\).
The relation \((\beta-3\gamma)p=2\beta\gamma\) gives \(b-3c=2bc\Rightarrow \dfrac1c-\dfrac3b=2\).

Let \(u=\dfrac1a,\ v=\dfrac1b,\ w=\dfrac1c\). Then \(v-2u=1\) and \(w-3v=2\). Since \(\dfrac1{x_i}=1+\dfrac1{(\text{ratio})}\), we get \(x_1=\dfrac1{u+1},\ x_3=\dfrac1{w+1}\).

From \(v=1+2u\), \(w=2+3v=5+6u\). Hence
\[\frac{P(B_1)}{P(B_3)}=\frac{x_1}{x_3}=\frac{w+1}{u+1}=\frac{6+6u}{1+u}=6.\]

For a solution to exist, \(\alpha\) must be at least the minimum of \(f(s)=\dfrac{4}{s}+\dfrac{1}{1-s}\) on \(s=\sin x\in(0,1)\).
\[f'(s)=-\frac{4}{s^2}+\frac{1}{(1-s)^2}=0\Rightarrow \frac{(1-s)^2}{s^2}=\frac14\Rightarrow \frac{1-s}{s}=\frac12\Rightarrow s=\frac23.\]
This is a minimum, and
\[f\!\left(\tfrac23\right)=\frac{4}{2/3}+\frac{1}{1/3}=6+3=9.\]
Thus the minimum value of \(\alpha\) is \(9\).

The given circle \(x^2+y^2-2x-6y+6=0\) has centre \(O_1=(1,3)\) and radius \(r=\sqrt{1+9-6}=2\).

A diameter of this circle is a chord of circle \(C\) with centre \(O_2=(2,1)\). The midpoint of that diameter is \(O_1=(1,3)\), which is the foot of the perpendicular from \(O_2\) to the chord, so the perpendicular distance is
\[d=|O_1O_2|=\sqrt{(2-1)^2+(1-3)^2}=\sqrt{5}.\]
Half the chord length equals the radius \(2\) of the first circle. Therefore the radius \(R\) of \(C\) satisfies
\[R^2=d^2+2^2=5+4=9\Rightarrow R=3.\]

The sum telescopes:
\[\sum_{r=1}^{n}\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{1}{1+r+r^2}\right)=\tan^{-1}(n+1)-\tan^{-1}(1).\]
As \(n\to\infty\), this tends to \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\dfrac{\pi}{4}=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\). Hence
\[\lim_{n\to\infty}\tan\{\cdots\}=\tan\frac{\pi}{4}=1.\]

\[\int_{-a}^{a}|x-2|\,dx=\int_{-a}^{2}(2-x)\,dx+\int_{2}^{a}(x-2)\,dx=\left(2+2a+\tfrac{a^2}{2}\right)+\left(\tfrac{a^2}{2}-2a+2\right)=a^2+4.\]
So \(\int_{-a}^{a}(|x|+|x-2|)\,dx=2a^2+4=22\Rightarrow a^2=9\Rightarrow a=3\).

Now \(\displaystyle\int_{3}^{-3}(x+\lfloor x\rfloor)\,dx=-\int_{-3}^{3}(x+\lfloor x\rfloor)\,dx\). Here \(\int_{-3}^{3}x\,dx=0\), and

Let \(z=x+iy\). Then \(|z-1|\) is real, so separating \(z+\alpha|z-1|+2i=0\) into real and imaginary parts:
\[y+2=0\Rightarrow y=-2,\qquad x+\alpha|z-1|=0.\]
With \(y=-2\), \(|z-1|=\sqrt{(x-1)^2+4}\), so \(x=-\alpha\sqrt{(x-1)^2+4}\). Squaring,
\[x^2=\alpha^2\big((x-1)^2+4\big)\Rightarrow (1-\alpha^2)x^2+2\alpha^2 x-5\alpha^2=0.\]
For a real \(x\) (a solution to exist), the discriminant must be \(\ge0\):
\[(2\alpha^2)^2-4(1-\alpha^2)(-5\alpha^2)=4\alpha^2(5-4\alpha^2)\ge0\Rightarrow \alpha^2\le\frac54.\]
Thus \(\alpha\in\left[-\tfrac{\sqrt5}{2},\tfrac{\sqrt5}{2}\right]\), so \(p=-\tfrac{\sqrt5}{2},\ q=\tfrac{\sqrt5}{2}\) and
\[4(p^2+q^2)=4\left(\tfrac54+\tfrac54\right)=10.\]

The sum of the diagonal entries of \(M^{\top}M\) is \(\operatorname{tr}(M^{\top}M)=\sum_{i,j}m_{ij}^2\), the sum of squares of all 9 entries. Each entry is \(0,1,\) or \(2\), contributing \(0,1,\) or \(4\). We need \(\sum m_{ij}^2=7\).

Let \(a\) entries equal \(2\) (each adds \(4\)) and \(b\) entries equal \(1\) (each adds \(1\)): \(4a+b=7\). Feasible: \((a,b)=(0,7)\) or \((1,3)\).

Case \((0,7)\): choose which 7 of 9 positions are \(1\): \(\binom{9}{7}=36\).
Case \((1,3)\): choose the position of the \(2\) in \(9\) ways, then \(3\) of the remaining \(8\) positions as \(1\): \(9\cdot\binom{8}{3}=9\cdot56=504\).

Total \(=36+504=540.\)
